solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carriage returns here for kind author

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A sentence about where a carriage turns round, seemingly for some friendly author.
explanation.walkthrough: The carriage is not a horse-drawn one: on the old office machine it was the moving part that carried the paper and was returned at each line's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The carriage return lever belonged to the old manual keyboard machine used for producing printed letters.

clue.text: Large bird boxes lean over

indicators.note: boxes means holds inside, as a container encloses its contents

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A big bird's cage tips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large bird' looks like one phrase, but Large supplies only L, which the bird boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To tilt is to slope or incline, the same as leaning over to one side.

clue.text: Woodworker collects new diary

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a planer is a tool or person that smooths wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter picks up a fresh diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner is a book or calendar for organising appointments, just as a diary is.

clue.text: We recruited nursing apprentices with good equipment

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the outer words cradle the inner letters

parts.note: taken as written
to recruit someone is to appoint them
an apprentice is a learner, L, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A hospital that took on trainee nurses is properly kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' suggests hospital care, but it means holding: the learners are cradled by the other words. Apprentices are learners, each L.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-appointed describes a room or building that is thoroughly furnished and fitted out.

clue.text: It can't hurt — it's not broken

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A reassuring line: there's no harm in it, since it still works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can't hurt' reads as a stock phrase, but 'hurt' is the anagram signal working on the letters of IT CAN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged, with no part missing, has not been broken.

clue.text: Spain allowed journalist to be brought out

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
licit means lawful or permitted
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter in Spain is permitted to be extracted from some situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or information, so something elicited has been drawn forth.

clue.text: Start to guzzle Polish food

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it

explanation.surface: Begin wolfing down Polish cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Dummy keepsake a priest nicked

indicators.note: nicked means cut into, so the priest's letter makes a cut inside

parts.note: a relic is an object kept in memory of the past

explanation.surface: A clergyman stole a mannequin souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' looks like stole but means cut: P goes into RELICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy is an imitation or copy of a real thing, which is what a replica is.

clue.text: Bum worker in debt

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom or behind
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A layabout labourer owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a tramp in American English; here it is the British word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means late or in arrears, especially with payments owed.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left ploughed

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or piece of grassland

indicators.note: ploughed earth is turned over and broken up, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: A stretch of meadow was left to be ploughed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like land, but it is a printed pamphlet; 'ploughed' rearranges LEFT into FLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political, the same kind of handout as a printed sheet.

clue.text: Thorough training of pathfinder gets this far

indicators.note: training puts the letters into a new order, like drilling recruits into formation

explanation.surface: Scout training gets this far and is thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange PATHFINDER; together with FAR (from 'this far'), it gives all the letters, so the answer is PATHFINDER less FAR, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is a detailed, comprehensive one.

clue.text: How to establish one's position on deck reading novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Reading a novel on deck while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being read, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigators without instruments estimate where they are from speed, heading and time elapsed using this method.

clue.text: Soldier with truck advanced across cold continent

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker of the ant colony

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the truck sits over the letter for cold

parts.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry
C is short for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A soldier drives a truck across a frozen landmass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is an ant here. ARTIC is the British short form of an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the southernmost landmass, the icy polar land around the South Pole.

clue.text: Popular northern flower

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A well-liked bloom from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword trick: something that flows, a river. The Inn flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inn is a European river, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Untidy, like monks with unacceptable habits?

definitions.meaning: monks belong to a religious order; misbehaving ones step outside its rules

explanation.surface: Messy, as monks behaving badly might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' are the monks' robes and also their behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a messy state and conduct breaking the rules of a religious order are described by this phrase.

clue.text: Developed in Peru but not yet edible

indicators.note: developed means changed into a new form, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Fruit grown in Peru that can't be eaten yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that has not matured is too green to eat.

clue.text: Carpet expert cuts hand

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the expert goes inside the other word

parts.note: to hand someone something is to reach it to them
a pro is an expert or professional

explanation.surface: A rug specialist slices his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is not a rug but a verb: to carpet someone is British slang for rebuking them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to summon them for a telling-off, a formal rebuke.

clue.text: Manage to gather jam at college

parts.note: a jam or fix is a scrape, a predicament
up means in residence at a university

explanation.surface: A student collects jam while at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' is a tight spot, not preserves.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape up money or support is to collect it with difficulty, from scattered sources.

clue.text: Homogeneous round baked food in pan

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the baked dish sits inside the face

parts.note: pan is slang for the face
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: A round pie baked in a pan is uniform throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' suggests cookware but is slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Things consistent in character, all of the same kind, are said to be of a piece.

clue.text: Bloke lives in hole in the wall, showing disbelief

indicators.note: in places the man and his existing inside the cash machine

parts.note: hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM
he refers to a man or bloke
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A man living in a hovel in a wall prompts incredulity.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hole in the wall' is a cash machine in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the lack of belief in any god.

clue.text: Show or hide rocks at bottom of mountain?

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose rocks on a slope

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Displaying or concealing the rubble at a mountain's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers both senses: to screen a film is to show it, and to screen a view is to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: Screen means both to project a film and to shield something from view.

clue.text: In Israel it is typically highbrow

indicators.note: In means the letters sit within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: In Israel, such things are usually intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: Highbrow and elitist both describe culture aimed at a select, sophisticated few.

clue.text: Prompt old archbishop is on his way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42

explanation.surface: A quick old cleric is climbing the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective (quick), but it is a noun or verb: a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a cue or sign to act, like a signal.

clue.text: Husband loves taking lead? How exciting!

indicators.note: taking lead means going first, so the loves come before the husband

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so loves gives two of them

explanation.surface: Is the husband letting love lead him?
explanation.definitionFit: Ooh is an exclamation of delight or excitement.

clue.text: Like Shakespearean fool's appalling old microphone

parts.note: tragic means dreadful or appalling
mic is short for microphone

explanation.surface: The jester's dreadful old microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fools blend humour with sorrow, mixing comedy and pathos.

clue.text: Go down to the audience together in this

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: to go down is to sink

explanation.surface: Performers descend to the stalls in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrase with the answer: 'in sync' means together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sync means moving or acting in step, in harmony.

clue.text: Arid wind leads palms to shrink

indicators.note: palms means conceals in the hand, so the letters are tucked inside

explanation.surface: A dry wind causes palm trees to wither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palms' looks like trees but means hides, as a conjuror palms a card.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to diminish gradually in size or number.

clue.text: Top seed stupid to ignore length with racket

parts.note: the top seed in a tournament is number one, written NO plus I

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: silly means stupid

explanation.surface: Tennis's top seed foolishly overlooks length with his racquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a tennis racquet but means din. NO 1 is read as NOI.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so doing something with one is doing it loudly.

clue.text: What's left after Potus loses his head?

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: POTUS is the President of the United States, here Trump

explanation.surface: A question about what remains after a president is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is the remnant of something, as in a rump parliament.

clue.text: A car with good quote has to be withdrawn, sorry

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A car with a fine price must be recalled; apologies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quote' looks like a price, but it means cite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry for a wrong is feeling regret, so expressing it is being remorseful.
